proof_boundary: This artifact is not a proof of an eventual sign, RH, or Lambda<=0. It exactly removes the Jordan-totient residue main term and identifies the remaining signed Mobius-error convolution and its inadequate absolute bound.

rows.formula: A_omega=1/((1+omega)zeta(1+2omega)); A_omega*x^(1+omega) is the residue main term of C_omega.
rows.proof_boundary: A residue main term is not a pointwise approximation with a signed remainder.
Definition of the signed summatory discrepancy.
Uses Suzuki's weight recursion and the level-zero weight.
Stieltjes/Abel summation only; no sign follows because W is signed.
The zero is the factor s-omega-1 at s=1+omega in the archimedean Mellin transform.
Integration by parts is valid because the endpoint products vanish.
The positive residue main term contributes exactly zero.
Exact reduction to a signed error convolution; it proves no positivity.
Both terms require Mobius cancellation and have no fixed sign.
Absolute-value estimate only; it discards all Mobius cancellation.

rows.formula: The elementary E bound and endpoint size W_(omega,k)(u)=O_(omega,k)(u^(omega-1)) give H_(omega,k)(x)=O_(omega,k)(x^(1/2-omega)*(1+log x)).
rows.proof_boundary: Far too large to establish eventual sign or the RH-conditional polylogarithmic scale.

rows.formula: Every finite k has the same near-zero power u^(omega-1), so logarithmic smoothing alone does not improve the exponent in the absolute-value bound.
rows.proof_boundary: Smoothing may improve cancellation, but not through a naive absolute estimate.

rows.formula: The Jordan-totient residue main term cannot be used as a positive dominant term because the Suzuki kernel annihilates it exactly.
rows.proof_boundary: Any proof claiming main-term domination fails this gate.

rows.formula: For one explicit omega_j->0 and selected k_j, prove that the signed convolution of E_(omega_j) with W_(omega_j,k_j) has one eventual sign, gaining beyond the O(x^(1/2-omega_j)log x) absolute barrier.
rows.proof_boundary: This cancellation estimate is not proved.
